summary:
Legrand S.A. is a French manufacturer of electrical and digital infrastructure for buildings, historically based in Limoges. Founded in 1865 as a porcelain workshop, it shifted into electrical equipment and focused exclusively on wiring devices after a 1949 factory fire. Its portfolio now includes more than 300,000 products, spanning switches and sockets, cable management, lighting controls, connected-home devices, EV charging and data-center systems.

The company expanded internationally through subsidiaries and acquisitions, beginning in Belgium in 1966 and later entering markets across Europe, the Americas, Asia and elsewhere. A proposed 2001 takeover by Schneider Electric failed after the European Commission raised competition concerns; Schneider had to sell its shares to investment firms KKR and Wendel. Legrand returned to the stock market in the following years and continued growing through acquisitions, particularly in data centers, connected products, energy efficiency, lighting, access systems and assisted living.

Legrand operates in 90 countries and sells products in nearly 180, with about 85% of sales generated internationally. It has eight production sites near its Limoges headquarters in France. The article identifies Benoît Coquart as general director from 2018 and Angeles Garcia-Poveda as chair of the board from 2020. Its competitors include Eaton, Hubbell, Leviton and Lutron.
